theory.intro: Compare fractions using equal-sized shapes divided into equal parts (area models), or by writing the fraction of each collection (discrete models). For equal-sized wholes, the larger shaded area represents the larger fraction. Count both the marked objects and the total when collections have different sizes.
facts: For a collection, write $\frac{\text{marked objects}}{\text{total objects}}$. Compare the marked counts directly only when the totals match. For different totals, use equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
steps: For area models, check that the wholes are equal-sized and each partition has equal parts. For collections, count the marked objects and the total objects.
Write the fractions. If the denominators differ, use equivalent fractions with a common denominator, subdividing the models when useful.
Compare the numerators once the denominators match. Write $<$, $>$ or $=$.

workedExamples.solution_text:
a. A has $1$ of $6$ equal parts shaded, so it shows $\frac{1}{6}$. B has $5$ of $6$ shaded, so it shows $\frac{5}{6}$.
$\frac{1}{6}<\frac{5}{6}$
B has the greater shaded fraction.
b. The shaded area depends on the size of the whole. Equal-sized bars let the shaded areas show the comparison of the fractions.

a. A has $4$ of $6$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{4}{6}$. B has $2$ of $3$ equal parts shaded: $\frac{2}{3}$.
Splitting each third of B into two equal parts gives $4$ shaded sixths.
$\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}$
The shaded areas are equal.
b. Two thirds equals A, so it is not greater. One third is smaller.
Three thirds gives $\frac{3}{3}=\frac{6}{6}>\frac{4}{6}$.
The least number is $3$ thirds.

P has $2$ marked counters out of $4$: $\frac{2}{4}$.
Q has $3$ marked counters out of $8$: $\frac{3}{8}$.
$\frac{2}{4}=\frac{4}{8}$
$\frac{4}{8}>\frac{3}{8}$
P has the greater marked fraction. Counting only marked counters is not enough because the totals differ.

workedExamples.question_text:
A collection has $20$ objects.
a. Represent $\frac{3}{5}$ of the collection and find how many objects are marked.
b. Write two equivalent fraction names for the marked part.

foundation.solution_text:
Bar A shows $\frac{2}{5}$ and bar B shows $\frac{4}{5}$.
$\frac{4}{5}>\frac{2}{5}$

foundation.question_text:
In two equal collections of $12$ counters, $3$ are red in collection P and $7$ are red in collection Q.
Compare the red fractions.

One equal-sized rectangle has $\frac{1}{3}$ shaded and another has $\frac{1}{6}$ shaded.
Which shaded area is larger?

A set has $8$ stars with $4$ coloured.
Another equal-sized set has $8$ stars with $6$ coloured.
Write and compare the fractions.
foundation.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{8}<\frac{6}{8}$
The second set has the greater coloured fraction.

foundation.question_text:
Two equal circles show $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$ shaded.
Which is greater?
True or false: in equal wholes, shading $2$ of $6$ equal parts is more than shading $1$ of $3$ equal parts.
foundation.solution_text:
$\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3}$
The statement is **false**; the areas are equal.

development.question_text:
Collection A has $5$ blue counters out of $10$.
Collection B has $3$ blue counters out of $5$.
Which has the greater blue fraction?
development.solution_text:
$\frac{3}{5}=\frac{6}{10}$
$\frac{6}{10}>\frac{5}{10}$
Collection B has the greater fraction.

development.question_text:
An area model split into twelfths has $8$ parts shaded.
Compare the shaded fractions with an equal-sized model split into thirds with $2$ parts shaded.

A student compares $3$ shaded counters out of $6$ with $4$ shaded counters out of $10$ and says the second is greater because $4>3$.
Correct the claim.
development.solution_text:
$\frac{3}{6}=\frac{5}{10}$
$\frac{5}{10}>\frac{4}{10}$
The first collection has the greater shaded fraction.

development.question_text:
Two equal strips are partitioned into eighths and quarters.
The first has $5$ eighths shaded.
What is the least number of quarters that must be shaded to represent a greater fraction?
development.solution_text:
$\frac{5}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{2}{4}=\frac{4}{8}$.
$\frac{3}{4}=\frac{6}{8}$ is greater.
$3$ quarters must be shaded.

development.question_text:
A bag model shows $6$ marked objects out of $15$.
Another shows $2$ marked out of $5$.
Compare the fractions.
Explain why area models must use equal-sized wholes when comparing $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$.
development.solution_text:
The shaded area depends on the size of the whole.
Equal-sized wholes let the fractions themselves determine the comparison.

mastery.question_text:
A collection has $18$ objects.
How many must be shaded to represent $\frac{2}{3}$?
Write two equivalent fraction names for the shaded part.

Equal-sized area models are divided into equal parts.
Model A has $9$ shaded parts out of $12$.
Model B has $7$ shaded parts out of $12$.
Which represents the greater fraction?
mastery.solution_text:
Both models are divided into twelfths.
$\frac{9}{12}>\frac{7}{12}$
Model A represents the greater fraction.

mastery.question_text:
Two equal-area rectangles are partitioned differently.
One shows $\frac{4}{6}$ shaded and the other $\frac{6}{9}$.
Decide whether either is greater.
mastery.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$
$\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$
Neither is greater; the shaded areas are equal.
